subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What trust model should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md skills before prompt loading and capability use?
rationale: The remaining work defines a security boundary for third-party instructions and affects existing skill compatibility, so automation cannot safely choose trust roots, revocation semantics, or unsigned default behavior.

options.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
options.body: Define signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory for now
options.body: Treat ClawHub verify output and install trust checks as user-visible advisory signals until maintainers choose a runtime enforcement contract.

options.title: Split design before implementation
options.body: Track issuer/signature format, ClawHub metadata, runtime loader checks, capability policy, and migration as separate owner-reviewed issues before code work.

recommendation.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
recommendation.body: Define signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and unsigned migration policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior security-product reviews and adjacent ClawHub trust-card work.
